title: Two occupations, many local societies
paragraphs: The line separated zones administered under different military authorities, but people did not cease to have family, economic, and cultural ties across it. Towns, transport routes, businesses, and households were drawn into arrangements that they had not designed. The division disrupted ways of moving and communicating that had previously crossed the peninsula.

Local politics also varied. Peoples committees and other organizations emerged or changed under the pressures of liberation. Policies pursued by occupation authorities interacted with these local circumstances, producing different institutional trajectories in north and south. A map with two colors can hide the density of this social experience.
